title: GPU onboarding cadence & regional heatmap (NA/EU/APAC) — sprint deck
content:
One-line summary:
Sprint-oriented, compact forecast mapping GPU onboarding cadence across North America, Europe, and APAC for May–Aug 2026. Focus: phased activation windows, utilization targets, hard/soft buffer, and sprint-lane sequencing to avoid cross-region supply spikes.

Purpose:
- Provide a runbook-ready cadence for infra and cloud ops to coordinate orders, reservation activations, and warm windows.
- Keep per-region utilization within 60–75% steady-state while preserving 20% active buffer for burst and failsafe.
- Sequence onboarding to minimize inter-region vendor capacity contention.

Key assumptions:
- Primary GPU type: A100-80GB (mix with a1.xlarge-like instances for warm lanes) and fallback q4-80 quantized variants.
- Customer demand growth scenario: steady +30% q/q for hosted inference route; 2x spike scenario modeled separately.
- Vendor lead windows: 4–6 weeks for reserved instances, 6–12 weeks for physical bare-metal procurement where applicable.
- Target steady-state utilization: 65% across active pools; soft buffer = 20% of total active GPUs; hard reserve = additional 10% capacity (warm but not active).

Compact onboarding table (columns: Region | Cloud zone | GPU type mix | May plan | Jun plan | Jul plan | Aug plan | Target util | Soft buffer | Rollout window | Milestones | Risk):
NA | us-west-2, us-east-1 | 70% A100-80GB / 30% H100-80GB + quantized variants | 120 GPUs | +180 GPUs | +240 GPUs | +120 GPUs | 65% | 20% | May–Aug (staggered sprints) | May wk2: reservation activation; Jun wk1: capacity smoke test; Jul wk3: traffic ramp to 60%; Aug wk2: full SLA baseline | medium (vendor lead risk + AZ throttling)
EU | eu-west-1, eu-central-1 | 80% A100-80GB / 20% T4-quant | 60 GPUs | +120 GPUs | +180 GPUs | +120 GPUs | 66% | 22% | May–Aug (delayed by 2 weeks vs NA) | May wk4: reserve commit; Jun wk3: deploy warm pool; Jul wk4: regional perf verification; Aug wk4: routing cutover | medium-high (customs/physical onboarding for on-prem partners)
APAC | ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1 | 60% A100-80GB / 40% mixed H100/T4 | 40 GPUs | +80 GPUs | +120 GPUs | +200 GPUs | 62% | 25% | Jun–Sep (shifted later to absorb supplier lead times) | Jun wk2: allocation request; Jul wk2: warm-up; Aug wk4: pilot customer traffic; Sep wk1: full throughput | high (supply + regional quotas)

Sprint-lane definitions (for infra ops cadence):
- Lane A (Fast activation): reservation-based cloud activations with immediate warm cache; target sprints: 2-week cycles, used primarily for NA core capacity.
- Lane B (Balanced): reserved + burstable instances, 3-week cycles, used for EU to smooth vendor contention.
- Lane C (Slow/Physical): bare-metal/partner on-prem activations, 4–6 week cycles, mainly APAC and strategic partner rollouts.

Heatmap intensity (how to read):
- Dark red = sprint concentration requiring vendor bottleneck coordination (avoid overlapping heavy lanes across regions).
- Amber = routine onboarding with standard lead times.
- Green = low-intensity warm window expansion.

Planned sprint calendar (sprint start = Monday):
- Sprint 1: 2026-05-04 — NA Lane A reservation activations (120 GPUs).
- Sprint 2: 2026-05-18 — EU Lane B reserve commit (60 GPUs) + NA warm tests.
- Sprint 3: 2026-06-01 — NA Lane A second wave (180 GPUs) + APAC Lane C allocation request.
- Sprint 4: 2026-06-15 — EU warm pool deploy (120 GPUs) + NA smoke tests.
- Sprint 5: 2026-06-29 — APAC onboarding (initial 80 GPUs) + NA optimization iteration.
- Sprint 6: 2026-07-13 — NA third wave (240 GPUs) + EU verification.
- Sprint 7: 2026-07-27 — EU finalization (180 GPUs) + APAC warm-up.
- Sprint 8: 2026-08-10 — APAC acceleration (200 GPUs) + global fallback drills.

Capacity math snapshot (May 31 & Aug 31 targets):
- May 31 total active GPUs planned: NA 300 / EU 180 / APAC 120 = 600 GPUs active. Soft buffer (20%) = 120 GPUs. Hard reserve (10%) = 60 GPUs. Total committed footprint ~780 GPUs.
- Aug 31 projected active: NA 660 / EU 480 / APAC 440 = 1580 GPUs active. Soft buffer (20%) = 316 GPUs. Hard reserve (10%) = 158 GPUs. Total committed footprint ~2054 GPUs.

Utilization & cost levers to watch (actionable):
- Increase batch size ceilings for background embeddings to lower token-per-GPU utilization by ~8–12% in steady-state. (Eng-serving-runtime action)
- Enable cross-region spillover only after warm pools reach 50% utilization to avoid cold-cache penalties. (Routing policy action)
- Short-term spot/reserved mix: target 10–15% spot for non-prod warm lanes to reduce cost without impacting SLA. (Infra finance)

Dependency list (critical path items):
- Reservation confirmations from cloud vendors (Jira ENGINFRA-4123).
- Terraform modules for instance sizing and GPU drivers (PR #89).
- Network peering approvals for EU and APAC interconnect (NetOps ticket NET-221).

Risks & mitigations matrix (short):
- Vendor lead delays: mitigation = reorder schedule with buffer lanes + vendor alternate pool (H100 fallback).
- Customs/onsite install delays (APAC bare-metal): mitigation = switch to reserved cloud lanes temporarily + increase soft buffer.
- Unexpected customer spike >2x: mitigation = immediate routing to dedicated reserved capacity and throttled degradation policy; notify SRE and CS.

Actions for next 7 days (owners):
- Confirm reservation windows with primary cloud vendor (Daniel Kim) — due 2026-02-27.
- Merge Terraform sizing PR and start dry-run in staging (Luis Martinez) — due 2026-03-03.
- Finalize APAC partner delivery SLA and customs checklist (Aisha Kapoor) — due 2026-03-05.
- Prepare communications for solutions engineering and account teams with expected warm/pilot windows (Priya Desai) — due 2026-03-02.
